feedback.problem:
A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(-1,0).$ Find the polar coordinates of $P.$ Give the polar angle in radians and do not round the answer.

The polar coordinates of $P$ are $(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies on the negative half of the $x$-axis, we have $\theta =\pi .$ 

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(1,\pi ).$
